abstract: H19 is one of the earliest discovered and most extensively studied lncRNAs, yet most studies have focused on the canonical 2,315-nt transcript arising from the IGF2/H19 locus on chromosome 11. We examined H19 isoform usage during the pluripotency-to-neuronal transition using NGN2/ASCL1-induced neurogenesis in KOLF2.1J human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). We show that a smaller, non-canonical isoform, variant 3, is the predominant H19 isoform in the pluripotent cells examined. This isoform lacks the large canonical promoter-derived exon 1 and contains a short, unique first exon encoded within the imprinting control region upstream of H19. Upon neuronal induction, isoform-specific RT-qPCR showed that variant 3 declined below the lower limit of reliable quantification (LLRQ) as canonical H19 and IGF2 mRNA increased. In contrast, human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells expressed canonical H19, while variant 3 remained below the LLRQ during neurogenic, osteogenic, and adipogenic differentiation. Independent FANTOM5 CAGE datasets supported transcription initiation in the predicted variant 3 promoter region in hiPSCs and human embryonic stem cells. Long-read RNA-seq identified transcripts linking the variant 3 first exon to downstream H19 exons. Public OCT4 and SOX2 ChIP-seq datasets showed recurrent peak overlap at the upstream OSM1 candidate region in pluripotent cells, with corresponding peaks absent in the differentiated datasets examined. Together, these findings support cell-state-associated regulation of the IGF2/H19 locus and identify alternative H19 isoform usage as a feature of human pluripotent cells.

summary: Wet-lab and public-data study showing H19 variant 3 is a pluripotency-associated non-canonical isoform that declines during neuronal differentiation in hiPSCs.
